# GrokMediaDownloader

> GrokMediaDownloader is a Chrome extension for Grok AI media management. Batch download images and videos, archive your entire Grok library organized by conversation, automate video generation with Video Gen Queue, create video stories with Story Mode, capture live streams in real-time, and organize everything into project folders — all processed locally in your browser with zero data collection. Published by Kario Studio. One-time $4.99 PRO lifetime license. Current version: 2.5.6.

## Key Features
- **Whole Library Download** (new in v2.5): Download every generated image and video in your Grok Imagine library, not just favorites. Files are grouped into one folder per conversation (named `yyyymmdd_prompt_shortID`) with filenames taken from the real generation prompt; video filenames match the generated list, carrying the same short-id suffix, and the per-folder `metadata.json` also records `userId`. Keeps its own download history separate from favorite and tag downloads. Free users can use this source for the last 7 days; PRO removes the time limit and adds date filtering
- **Three Download Sources**: Favorite (liked items), Tag (one Grok tag/folder, output under `tags/{tagName}/`), and All Generated Media by Conversation. Each source has independent deduplication records. Since v2.5.1 the source selector is free for all users and defaults to the whole library
- **1080p Support** (new in v2.5): 1080p is a distinct quality tier alongside SD and HD/720p. Downloads take the highest available quality; upgrades move one tier at a time (SD→HD, 720p/HD→1080p). 1080p upgrade requires a SuperGrok Heavy plan and an explicit opt-in that is off by default
- **Batch Download**: Scan and download all Grok AI images and videos at once with smart filtering by date, type, and resolution
- **Video Gen Queue**: Automate video generation by queuing multiple image posts — the extension auto-generates videos in the background
- **Story Mode**: Merge multiple Grok video clips into a single MP4 using in-browser WebAssembly FFmpeg — no server upload needed
- **Stream Capture**: Real-time DOM observer detects and queues newly generated images as you browse Grok AI
- **Project Download**: Group source images and resulting videos into organized project folders for bulk export
- **HD Upgrade**: Scan favorites or your whole library for videos below the top quality tier and send upgrade requests via the Grok API
- **Tag Download** (rebuilt in v2.5.2, completed in v2.5.6): Grok's August tag migration left content stranded in both its old and its new tag store, so tag lists and tag contents are now the union of the two — newly created tags, the full contents of old tags, and tags that exist only in the old system all download again. v2.5.3 and v2.5.4 added tag list/content pagination fixes and full scan diagnostics so accounts with many tags also see the older ones. Tag downloads support prompt-based filenames, where videos use their own animation prompt, or the source image's

## Compatibility Note
In July 2026 Grok migrated to a new conversation-and-asset media backend. Extension versions before 2.5.0 cannot detect images and videos generated after that migration, and the legacy Favorite source no longer receives newly generated media at all — a Favorite scan can come back empty and HD upgrade can wrongly report that every video is already upgraded. Version 2.5.1 makes the whole library the default source for both downloading and upgrading. Grok also rebuilt tags as collections, but that migration is incomplete in both directions — content is stranded in the old tag store as well as the new one, and each side holds tags the other lacks; version 2.5.2 read only the new store, while version 2.5.6 reads both and merges them, so every tag and its full contents are listed again. Since September 2026 Grok no longer returns prompts with the media list, so versions before 2.5.6 write filenames, folder names and metadata without the real prompt; 2.5.6 recovers each prompt from the conversation that generated the media (videos use their own animation prompt, or the source image's), caches it persistently so a whole-library regenerate drops from minutes to seconds, and fetches prompts only when the filename or metadata settings require them. After updating, reload the extension at chrome://extensions, refresh the Grok tab, and regenerate the download list once so the new naming rules apply.

## Stats
- 4,000+ active users
- 4.1/5 rating (24 reviews) on Chrome Web Store
- Available in 6 languages: English, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Spanish, German

## Technical
- 100% client-side processing (WebAssembly FFmpeg, IndexedDB, Chrome Side Panel API)
- No data collection, no server uploads
- Works with Grok AI (grok.com / x.ai)
